entry.question:
## Physical scenario

A deep-sea diver is suspended beneath the surface of Loch Ness by a \( 100\text{-m} \)-long cable that is attached to a boat on the surface (\textbf{figure}). The diver and his suit have a total mass of \( 120\,\text{kg} \) and a volume of \( 0.0800\,\text{m}^3 \). The cable has a diameter of \( 2.00\,\text{cm} \) and a linear mass density of \( \mu = 1.10\,\text{kg/m} \). The diver thinks he sees something moving in the murky depths and jerks the end of the cable back and forth to send transverse waves up the cable as a signal to his companions in the boat.

## Question

What is the tension in the cable at its lower end, where it is attached to the diver?

## Answer choices

- A: A: 392N

- B: B: 452N

- C: C: 332N

- D: D: 372N

## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image depicts a person in a diving suit submerged underwater. They are connected to the surface by a blue rope or line. There are two measurements indicated with arrows: one labeled "100 m" from the surface to the diver and another labeled "x," extending from a point on the rope to the diver. The text "m = 120 kg" is written next to the diver, indicating the mass of the person and equipment. The scene is set in water, indicated by the blue background.
